sections.label: Your situation
sections.intro: Two practical questions. They help me arrange results; no career is ever hidden.

questions.prompt: Which best describes where you are in your studies?

options.label: Science with Physics, Chemistry and Maths (PCM)
options.nova: Science with Maths opens engineering, architecture, aviation and much more. I will use this only to order your results, never to hide a career.

options.label: Science with Physics, Chemistry and Biology (PCB)
options.nova: PCB is the usual starting point for medicine, nursing, pharmacy and the life sciences. It only helps me order your results.

options.label: Commerce
options.nova: Commerce leads toward accounting, finance, business and law, and many other doors stay open too.

options.label: Arts or Humanities
options.nova: Arts and Humanities open law, civil services, teaching, media, design and more.

options.label: Diploma or ITI
options.nova: Diploma and ITI are strong routes into skilled technical work. I will flag the careers that usually start there.

options.label: I already have a graduate degree
options.nova: Thanks. Next I will ask your field, so I can place your degree.

options.label: Engineering or technology
options.nova: An engineering or technology degree. Noted; many technical and management routes build on it.

options.label: Science
options.nova: A science degree. Noted; it is a base for research, health, technology and teaching routes.

options.label: Commerce or management
options.nova: Commerce or management. Noted; finance, business and public-service routes build on it.

options.label: Arts or humanities
options.nova: Arts or humanities. Noted; law, policy, media, teaching and counselling routes build on it.

options.label: Law
options.nova: A law degree. Noted; legal and policy routes start right there.

options.label: Medicine or health sciences
options.nova: A health sciences degree. Noted; clinical and health-system routes start from here.

options.label: Design or architecture
options.nova: A design or architecture degree. Noted; creative and built-environment routes start from here.

questions.prompt: Which of these would you enjoy on a free weekend?

options.label: Fixing or building something with tools
options.nova: Fixing and building with your hands is a classic Realistic signal.

options.label: Figuring out how something works
options.nova: Wanting to know how things work is Investigative thinking.

options.label: Drawing, designing or making something creative
options.nova: Making something creative points to the Artistic side.

options.label: Helping someone with a problem
options.nova: Helping someone through a problem is a Social strength.

options.label: Organising an outing or event for a group
options.nova: Getting a group moving is Enterprising: leading and organising.

options.label: Putting your notes, files or room in order
options.nova: Liking things in order is a Conventional signal.

questions.prompt: In a school or college project, which part would you grab?

options.label: Building the model or setting up the equipment
options.nova: Setting up the build is Realistic: practical and hands-on.

options.label: Researching and analysing the data
options.nova: Digging into the data is Investigative.

options.label: Designing the presentation and visuals
options.nova: Shaping how it looks is Artistic.

options.label: Helping teammates who are stuck
options.nova: Supporting teammates is a Social habit worth noting.

options.label: Presenting and persuading the audience
options.nova: Winning an audience over is Enterprising.

options.label: Keeping the schedule and references in order
options.nova: Keeping a project on track is Conventional: dependable and exact.

questions.prompt: Which kind of daily work sounds best?

options.label: Operating machinery or working outdoors
options.nova: Machines and open air: Realistic.

options.label: Running experiments and testing ideas
options.nova: Testing ideas is the heart of Investigative work.

options.label: Writing, filming or performing for an audience
options.nova: Creating for an audience is Artistic.

options.label: Teaching or caring for people
options.nova: Teaching and caring sit at the centre of Social work.

options.label: Selling, negotiating or leading a team
options.nova: Selling, negotiating and leading: Enterprising.

options.label: Preparing accurate reports, accounts or records
options.nova: Accuracy with reports and records is Conventional.

questions.prompt: At a college fest, what would you volunteer for?

options.label: Setting up the stage, lights and sound
options.nova: Rigging and setting up is practical, Realistic work.

options.label: Running the quiz or science exhibition
options.nova: A quiz or exhibition suits Investigative curiosity.

options.label: Designing posters or performing on stage
options.nova: Posters and performance are Artistic.

options.label: Welcoming visitors and helping them find their way
options.nova: Welcoming people is a Social instinct.

options.label: Raising sponsorship and promoting the fest
options.nova: Raising sponsorship takes Enterprising drive.

options.label: Managing the budget, tickets and registrations
options.nova: Budgets and registrations are Conventional strengths.

questions.prompt: Which story would you rather read?

options.label: How a bridge, engine or aircraft was built
options.nova: Curiosity about how big things are built is Realistic.

options.label: A new scientific or medical discovery
options.nova: A discovery story pulls on Investigative interest.

options.label: How a film, album or fashion line was created
options.nova: Creative-process stories are Artistic.

options.label: A teacher or doctor who changed lives
options.nova: Stories about changing lives point to Social interests.

options.label: How a founder built a company
options.nova: Founder stories are Enterprising.

options.label: How a bank or tax system keeps things running
options.nova: Interest in how systems stay orderly is Conventional.

questions.prompt: Which skill would you most like to be great at?

options.label: Fixing or operating anything mechanical
options.nova: Mechanical know-how is Realistic.

options.label: Solving problems others find too hard
options.nova: Hard problems attract Investigative minds.

options.label: Creating things people find beautiful or moving
options.nova: Making beautiful or moving things is Artistic.

options.label: Understanding and supporting people
options.nova: Understanding people is the Social core.

options.label: Persuading people and making decisions
options.nova: Persuading and deciding: Enterprising.

options.label: Being precise and dependable with details
options.nova: Precision and dependability are Conventional.

questions.prompt: Which project would you start yourself?

options.label: Growing a garden or looking after animals
options.nova: Plants and animals are classic Realistic territory.

options.label: Finding out why something keeps going wrong
options.nova: Chasing the cause of a problem is Investigative.

options.label: Starting a blog, channel or band
options.nova: Starting something creative is Artistic.

options.label: Tutoring younger students
options.nova: Tutoring others is Social.

options.label: Starting a small business or fundraiser
options.nova: A business or fundraiser is Enterprising.

options.label: Building a budget or timetable that really works
options.nova: A budget or timetable that works is Conventional.

questions.prompt: In a team, you are usually the one who…

options.label: gets hands-on and makes it work
options.nova: Making it work with your hands is Realistic.

options.label: asks why and checks the facts
options.nova: Asking why and checking facts is Investigative.

options.label: comes up with the original idea
options.nova: Original ideas are Artistic.

options.label: makes sure everyone feels included
options.nova: Making everyone feel included is Social.

options.label: takes charge and drives the decision
options.nova: Taking charge is Enterprising.

options.label: makes sure it is done properly and on time
options.nova: Doing it properly and on time is Conventional.

questions.prompt: Which school subjects do you enjoy most?
questions.hint: Pick up to 3. How each subject counts toward the six interest types is our own weighting, not O*NET's.

options.label: Mathematics
options.nova: Maths feeds both Investigative problem-solving and Conventional precision.

options.label: Physics
options.nova: Physics blends Investigative curiosity with a Realistic feel for how things work.

options.label: Chemistry
options.nova: Chemistry is a straight Investigative signal.

options.label: Biology
options.nova: Biology leans Investigative, and often Social through health and care.

options.label: Computer science
options.nova: Computer science mixes Investigative thinking with Conventional logic and order.

options.label: Economics, accountancy or business studies
options.nova: Business subjects point to Enterprising and Conventional interests.

options.label: History, civics or political science
options.nova: These subjects lean Social and Investigative: people, society and evidence.

options.label: Geography
options.nova: Geography combines a Realistic liking for the outdoors with Investigative curiosity.

options.label: English or other languages and literature
options.nova: Language and literature lean Artistic and Social: expression and people.

options.label: Art, design, music or drama
options.nova: Creative subjects are a strong Artistic signal.

options.label: Physical education or sports
options.nova: Sport mixes Realistic physical activity with Social teamwork.

options.label: Psychology or sociology
options.nova: Psychology and sociology lean Social and Investigative.

questions.prompt: Where do you do your best work?

options.label: On my own, with few interruptions
options.nova: Quiet focus time matters to you. I will look for work that leaves room for it.

options.label: With a small team I know well
options.nova: A small team you trust is how a lot of careers actually work.

options.label: Around lots of people, talking and coordinating
options.nova: You gain energy from people. Plenty of careers are built around exactly that.

questions.prompt: How do you feel about pressure and deadlines?

options.label: I prefer a steady pace without big deadlines
options.nova: A steady pace is a perfectly good preference, and many careers run that way.

options.label: A bit of pressure helps me focus
options.nova: A little pressure to sharpen you is normal in most careers.

options.label: I enjoy fast, high-stakes situations
options.nova: You like fast, high-stakes work. Some careers are built around it.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer clear instructions or freedom to decide?

options.label: Clear steps and instructions
options.nova: You like clear steps. Careers with set procedures and standards will suit that.

options.label: A mix of both
options.nova: A mix of both keeps your options wide.

options.label: Freedom to decide how and what to do
options.nova: You want room to decide. Some careers give far more of that than others.

options.label: At a desk or screen
options.nova: Desk and screen work is where many careers live.

options.label: A mix of desk work and moving around
options.nova: A mix of sitting and moving suits a wide range of work.

options.label: Hands-on, moving around, or outdoors
options.nova: Hands-on and on your feet: some careers are mostly that.

questions.prompt: Are you open to 5 or more years of study before a full-time job?

options.label: Yes, I am open to 5 or more years
options.nova: Good. That keeps long professional routes such as medicine, law and architecture in your strongest list.

options.label: No, I would rather start working sooner
options.nova: Noted. Careers with a long study route will move to Explore further, still visible, with the reason.

options.label: I am not sure yet
options.nova: That is fine. I will not flag anything on study length for now.

questions.prompt: Do you need to start earning soon?

options.label: Yes, I need to start earning soon
options.nova: Understood. I will point out careers that usually need several years of study before a full-time role. None are hidden.

options.label: No, I can take my time
options.nova: Then I will not flag longer routes on that account.

options.label: I am not sure
options.nova: No problem. I will not assume anything.
